text: Atlas of Extra Gravitation
finding: The site name, shown on every page, states that there is extra gravitation. The Atlas's own data include systems where g_obs/g_bar is at or below 1 (e.g. globular clusters such as NGC 362, ratio 0.41), so the name presumes the result the site says it only describes. Recorded once here; it applies site-wide.

text: Above it, more acceleration is observed than the detected baryons predict.
finding: The 'How to read' list explains points on and above the line but never says what points below it mean, although plotted measurements lie below it (e.g. NGC 362 at g_obs/g_bar = 0.41). Reading guidance only for the excess side frames the chart as a picture of excess; add the below-the-line case in both layers.

text: Above the line, the pull is stronger than that.
finding: Plain-layer counterpart of the same omission: no sentence for points below the line.

text: An open atlas of the acceleration discrepancy: where and how the observed gravitational acceleration exceeds what Newtonian gravity predicts from detected baryonic matter
finding: The opening definition describes the Atlas as a map of where g_obs exceeds g_bar. Methods says absence of the discrepancy is shown as prominently as its presence; the definition should cover both (where and how g_obs differs from g_bar). Plain line 'things are pulled harder than Newton's gravity' has the same framing.

text: Famaey & McGaugh 2012, Living Reviews in Relativity 15, 10
finding: The only two reviews listed ('organised around one account of the discrepancy' and 'successes and failures of one account') both concern the same single account, and most 'Several kinds of system on one plot' entries come from the same research group. The selection gives one account's literature the visible review slot; add reviews organised around other accounts (the changelog shows five field reviews were read, including Cirelli, Strumia & Zupan 2026) or remove the review list.

text: The relation taken to one new kind of system
finding: The sub-heading presumes that a single relation exists and is being extended to new systems. That is a result claimed by some authors, not a neutral description. Use a heading such as 'The g_obs-g_bar comparison for one kind of system'.

text: It had been switched on by our web host without our noticing; this is now fixed and disclosed.
finding: The plain layer says the analytics issue is 'now fixed', which reads as if the counter was switched off. The technical layer says the counter is active for all countries and only the disclosure was corrected. The plain layer also leaves out the referrer and device type that the technical layer lists.

text: extra pull (observed pull ÷ pull from detected matter; 1 = equal, below 1 = less)
finding: The plain name for g_obs/g_bar is 'extra pull', so a ratio of 1 or below 1 is still called 'extra pull'. The label carries the result (an excess). The expert term 'acceleration discrepancy' does not have this problem. Suggest 'pull ratio' or 'observed ÷ detected'. The same applies to the Methods 'What is measured' entry 'Extra pull : observed pull ÷ pull from detected matter'.

text: 175 spinning disc galaxies. The observed pull comes from how fast stars and gas go round; the pull from detected matter comes from the starlight and the hydrogen gas.
finding: The technical layer says the gas mass includes the 1.33 helium factor. The plain layer says 'the hydrogen gas' only. The SPARC methods page plain layer does mention helium, so this summary is inconsistent with it.

text: A candidate can be plotted only if it has at least two bins and its light coverage (§4, step 4) is at least 0.80.
finding: Light coverage is continuous, and a fixed 0.80 cut decides whether a cluster appears on the map (Crater fails it). The page gives no reason or source for the value. State the ruling and the reason on the page, or show coverage as a continuous property of the plotted points.

text: because their sources describe them as possibly out of equilibrium
finding: The site's equilibrium rule (D-097, as given in the changelog) keeps a system plotted when its source states only a possibility, and excludes it on a firm statement. The changelog calls NGC 2298 and Pal 5 'findings'. The Reproduction page's plain layer says their sources 'say they are being pulled apart'. These three wordings disagree on why the two clusters are off the map.

text: Geha 2026 ApJ 999 140 (arXiv 0706.0516v2), p9, Table 3, row Canes Venatici I.
finding: The source route is self-contradictory: a 2026 paper is paired with a 2007 arXiv identifier. The same mismatch appears on Canes Venatici II, Coma Berenices, Leo IV and Leo T. A reader following the route cannot tell which document holds the value.

text: Kvasova 2024 ApJ 972 180 (arXiv 1112.1067v3), p9, Table 3, row And XVIII, column σLOS.
finding: The citation names Kvasova 2024, but the arXiv identifier and place (1112.1067v3, Table 3, σLOS) are those of Tollerud 2012, used for the other Andromeda rows. Other rows show similar label/identifier mismatches: 'Collins 2013 ApJ 768 172 (arXiv 2505.04475v3)' (And VI, And XXIII), 'Collins 2013 ApJ 768 172 (arXiv 1910.12879v2)', 'Battaglia 2011 MNRAS 411 1013 (arXiv 2504.02787v1)', 'Gregory 2019 MNRAS 485 2010 (arXiv 2001.11410v1)' and 'Ou 2024 ApJ 966 33 (arXiv 0706.0516v2)'. The visible route to the source for these values is wrong or ambiguous.

text: A problem with this dataset is recorded here. The technical view gives the details and the evidence.
finding: For issues #222, #225, #227, #232 and #234 the plain layer points to the technical view, but the technical view says only 'The description is on GitHub (linked below).', and GitHub could not be reached at build time. Neither layer describes these five issues on the page, and for the others the expert layer carries no description at all.

text: A5 Dwarf spheroidal and ultra-faint (49) and A7 Unusual configurations (7)
finding: A7 is defined as 'Galaxies in unusual configurations: tidal dwarf galaxies, polar-ring galaxies'. Here it also holds Local Group dwarfs (and, elsewhere, Crater and lenses whose readers disagreed, marked 'A7, ambiguous'). The A7 row of the kinds table does not say it also holds systems whose kind is ambiguous or rests on dynamics, so the category name misdescribes its members. Add an explicit 'kind not settled' category or state the rule in the A7 row.

text: what it explains and what it does not yet explain
finding: The plain template says each account will list what it 'does not yet explain'. 'Yet' presumes the account will eventually explain it. The technical template says neutrally 'the Atlas measurements it addresses, and those it does not'. The plain layer should match.

text: KiDS-1000 weak-lensing radial acceleration relation: stacked isolated lenses
finding: The dataset title states that the data form a 'relation'. That is the source paper's framing, but used as the Atlas's own dataset label it carries a result. The same title is repeated on the KiDS dataset page and the Reproduction page. Suggest 'KiDS-1000 weak-lensing g_obs against g_bar: stacked isolated lenses', with the source's title kept in the citation.

text: All checks passed. Nothing changed in the numbers; what is new is the record of where each one comes from. The current cluster version: the same numbers, now each tied to a cited, checked source.
finding: The technical layer beside it says 'Part A's failures and part B's pass stand as reported for v2', and the Reproduction page's plain layer says 'Some file checks failed; the package passed'. The plain statement 'All checks passed' misreports a test result.

text: Version 2 uses the values the authors released in 2022, so its numbers differ from version 1.
finding: On the v3 page the plain layer talks about 'Version 2', but the technical layer says 'X-COP v3 re-issues v2'. The plain layer should name the current version.

text: All checks passed. Nothing changed in the numbers; what is new is the record of where each one comes from. The current SPARC version: the same numbers, now each tied to a cited, checked source.
finding: The technical layer says the 4 points of issue #8 remain flagged, and the comparison with the authors' RAR file (failed, 4 points) still applies. The plain summary leaves out the standing mismatch. Add it, as the Reproduction page's plain layer does.

text: Our own tables may be reused with credit, unless the original study’s terms say otherwise.
finding: The technical layer says 'Atlas tables intended CC BY 4.0 under D-004; to be confirmed against the terms of the CDS/VizieR record ... (issue #9)'. The plain layer presents reuse as settled. The same plain sentence appears on every dataset page, where the technical layer says 'intended'.

text: Hot gas: absent, or modelled (the authors' assumed halo, hot-gas variant only; D-034)
finding: 'Halo' is used as description in Atlas text, against the vocabulary rule. Here it means the authors' assumed hot-gas component, but the word is not needed. Also 'plus an assumed hot-gas halo for the variant' and 'for the hot-gas rows, the assumed halo'. The changelog says this wording would change at re-issue, but it remains in v3. Use 'assumed hot-gas component', as the site text already does elsewhere.

text: Lower panel: the pull from detected matter as a share of the observed pull
finding: The 'Pull budget' chart and the table column g_bar / g_obs (shown as %, e.g. 47%) present the detected-matter pull as a share of a total, with the rest left implicitly unaccounted for. 'Budget' and 'share' frame g_obs as a sum in which part is missing, which leans towards a component (missing-matter) reading. Values above 100% (e.g. 130%) show the framing does not fit. (Label text is from the page's chart script, site/_astro/budget.DUfZZWW5.js.) Use a neutral ratio label (g_obs/g_bar is already given) and a neutral title such as 'Observed and detected-matter pull'. The same chart is on aeg-s-000124, and the map links to it as 'pull budget'.

text: How tilted the disc is as we see it. It changes the observed pull of the whole galaxy at once. It can be changed with a slider on the map.
finding: The plain layer says inclination (and distance) can be changed 'with a slider on the map'. The technical layer and the map itself say these are set per galaxy on the galaxy's own page. The plain distance text also says it 'changes the pulls of the whole system', but the technical layer says g_bar is distance-independent and only g_obs moves. The same plain text is on aeg-s-000124 and the SPARC dataset page.

text: stellar mass not in the source; g_bar bounded below by gas only; recorded under
finding: The plain layer says 'for the reason below', but the reason is given only in technical wording. There is no plain version of why the cluster is off the map. The same applies to aeg-s-000187.

text: globular cluster, Milky Way. Stellar velocity dispersion at the half-light radius (dynamics). Recorded, not plotted.
finding: Crater is labelled a globular cluster in both layers ('An old, dense ball of stars in our galaxy'), but the page's own reason is 'classification disputed by sources: A7, ambiguous'. Whether Crater is a cluster or a galaxy is disputed in the literature partly on dynamical grounds, so the header label takes a side the page says is open.

text: classification disputed by sources: A7, ambiguous (D-038 4A)
finding: The not-plotted reasons appear under the plain heading 'Why:' only in technical shorthand (e.g. 'no Harris (2010) horizontal-branch distance (D-042)'). There is no plain version.

text: Mass that bends the light, inside the ring
finding: The plain label states as fact that a mass bends the light. M_E is the mass that GR lensing on the declared reference would need, so calling it 'mass that bends the light' and setting it against 'Detected matter' presumes the difference is unseen mass. The Methods page rejects 'mass discrepancy' for exactly this reason. Suggest 'Mass needed to bend the light this much (GR)'.

text: Kind used for this lens: A7, ambiguous: the two readings of the kind differ (not adjudicated; SECOND_READING.md).
finding: Reader disagreement places the lens in A7 'Galaxies in unusual configurations', which is a physical kind (tidal dwarfs, polar rings). The label then carries a claim that the readers did not make. Use a separate 'kind not settled' value.

text: Extra pull (log of observed ÷ detected)
finding: The plain axis label of the Ratio view calls log(g_obs/g_bar) 'Extra pull', including the values below zero (less pull than detected matter gives). The label carries the result. The technical label 'acceleration discrepancy' does not. The Scale/Distance view's plain axis 'Extra pull (log)' has the same problem. (Labels are from the map page's inline chart configuration.)

text: Mass implied by the observed pull against the detected mass
finding: The plain Mass view says the observed pull 'implies' a mass ('Implied mass'), which presents the discrepancy as mass. The technical layer calls it a spherical-equivalent enclosed mass and a convention. The plain layer should say it is the mass Newton's law would need, a way of writing the pull, not a measured mass.

text: Its own page shows how much of its pull Newton’s gravity from the detected matter matches.
finding: The plain text describes the system page as showing 'how much of its pull' detected matter matches, a share or budget framing. The technical text says only 'its page holds the pull budget'. Both lean on the budget framing found on the system pages.

text: two clusters kept on record but off the charts because their sources say they are being pulled apart
finding: The plain layer states a firmer reason ('being pulled apart') than the technical layer ('recorded, not plotted, with the source's quotation') and the GC methods page ('possibly out of equilibrium'). The plain claim should match what the sources are quoted as saying.

text: Putman et al. 2021 Table 1, None
finding: The source shown for the gas-limit input (3200 solMass) is 'Table 1, None', with no row. The route to the value is incomplete on the page. Known issue #232 records the cause and the changelog says the locator was corrected, but the visible source text still reads 'None'. Show the galaxy's row, as the locator now gives it.
